name: backlog
title: Repo Backlog
purpose: A durable in-repo store for future work items that are not yet ready for an active Epic or change. Items are JSONL-encoded, git-tracked, branch-local, and promotable to either an ADV change or an Epic shell entry.

requirements.title: Backlog Lives In-Repo and Is Branch-Local
requirements.body: The backlog MUST be stored as `.adv/backlog.jsonl` inside the project repository. The file MUST be git-tracked and branch-local so that disjoint sets of future work items can coexist on different branches and merge through `merge=union`. The backlog MUST remain readable and writable from any worktree checked out from the same repository.

scenarios.title: Backlog file is created on first add
given: A project with no existing backlog
then: `.adv/backlog.jsonl` is created
The file contains a header line with `schemaVersion` followed by the new item

scenarios.title: Backlog survives worktree switches
given: A backlog file exists on the current branch
scenarios.when: A different worktree checks out the same branch
then: The backlog file is present with identical content
Items can be read and appended from the new worktree

requirements.title: Backlog Is a Structured JSONL Stream
requirements.body: The backlog file MUST contain a single header line with a `schemaVersion` field, followed by zero or more JSON-encoded backlog items, one per line. Append is the only write path for normal additions. Each line MUST be independently parsable and Zod-validated against the backlog item schema. Malformed lines MUST be surfaced as typed errors rather than silently dropped.

scenarios.title: Valid backlog parses completely
given: A backlog file with a header and several items
then: All valid items are returned
The header schema version is preserved

scenarios.title: Malformed line returns typed error
given: A backlog file containing one invalid JSON line
then: Valid items are still returned
The malformed line is reported with line number, raw content, and parse error

requirements.title: Backlog Items Have a Simple Lifecycle
requirements.body: Each backlog item MUST carry a `status` of either `active` or `archived`. Archiving is a soft-delete that records `archived_at`. Active items are the default read surface. Items MAY record `promoted_to` when they are promoted to a change or Epic shell entry. Promotion does not delete the backlog line; it appends an updated record so the latest item wins.

scenarios.title: Archive soft-deletes an item
then: A new record is appended with `status: archived`
`archived_at` is set to the current ISO timestamp
The original line remains in the file

scenarios.title: Promotion records target identity
then: A new record is appended with `promoted_to.kind` and `promoted_to.id`
`promoted_to.promoted_at` records the promotion time

requirements.title: Promotion Is Idempotent and Typed
requirements.body: Promoting a backlog item to an ADV change or Epic shell entry MUST be idempotent on the tuple `(itemId, targetId)`. Re-promoting the same item to the same target MUST return the existing promotion without creating duplicate records. Promotion to a different target MUST append a new promoted record. Promotion of an archived item MUST be refused.

scenarios.title: Re-promotion is idempotent
given: An active item already promoted to change `addFoo`
scenarios.when: The same item is promoted to `addFoo` again
then: No new backlog line is written
The existing promotion record is returned

scenarios.title: Archived promotion is refused
scenarios.when: A caller attempts to promote it
then: The operation fails with a typed `archived` error
No mutation is written

requirements.title: Archive State Is Respected by Reads
requirements.body: Default backlog reads MUST return only `active` items. Callers MAY request archived items explicitly. Adding a new item whose current latest state is archived MUST reactivate it (append a new `active` record). Promoting an archived item MUST be refused.

scenarios.title: Default list excludes archived items
given: A backlog with one active and one archived item
then: Only the active item is returned

scenarios.title: Adding an archived item reactivates it
given: An item whose latest record is archived
scenarios.when: A caller adds the same item id again
then: A new active record is appended
Subsequent reads return the item as active

requirements.title: Backlog Schema Version Is Explicit and Migrated
requirements.body: The backlog header MUST declare a `schemaVersion`. Schema migrations MUST be hand-rolled per version (explicit branching), not a generic Zod passthrough. Writing to a backlog whose schema version is older than the current code version MUST be refused unless the caller explicitly consents to an automatic migration.

scenarios.title: Header declares schema version
then: The first line is a valid header
`schemaVersion` equals the current version

scenarios.title: Writes against old schema are refused
scenarios.when: A caller attempts to append without migration consent
then: The operation fails with a typed `schema_version` error
No line is appended

requirements.title: Concurrent Appends Are Serialized
requirements.body: Concurrent worktrees or processes appending to `.adv/backlog.jsonl` MUST use a file lock to prevent interleaved writes. Reads MAY proceed without a lock. The lock implementation MUST handle stale locks from dead processes.

scenarios.title: Concurrent adds do not corrupt JSONL
then: Every line is valid JSON
No line is interleaved or truncated

requirements.title: Epic Shell Entries Can Import Backlog Items
requirements.body: An Epic shell entry MAY carry a `backlog_ref` linking it to a repo backlog item. When a shell is created from a backlog reference, the shell title and success hint MAY be derived from the backlog item, and the shell MUST record `imported_from: { backlog_id, imported_at }` provenance. Imported shells are one-way bound: subsequent edits to the backlog item do not update the shell.

scenarios.title: Shell derived from backlog item carries provenance
given: A backlog item with title and success hint
then: The shell entry title and success hint match the backlog item
`imported_from.backlog_id` is set
`imported_from.imported_at` is set

scenarios.title: Imported shell is one-way bound
given: A shell imported from a backlog item
scenarios.when: The backlog item title is updated
then: The shell title remains unchanged
